items.prompt: A retailer compares two designs for product questions. An efficient retrieval workflow measures 1.8 seconds p95 and meets the unit-cost budget; an agentic workflow measures 6.4 seconds p95 and exceeds it. Which initial decision aligns the solution with value?
constraints: The service has a latency and unit-cost target.
Both candidates need task-quality evidence and staff escalation remains available.

options.text: Choose the agentic design because more autonomous steps signal greater transformation even though its measured latency and cost miss the target.
Choose the efficient design solely from price and skip quality measurement because retrieval is already familiar.
Run both designs for every customer and let answer length determine which one creates more value.
Use the efficient candidate for routine questions, verify its quality on representative cases, and route measured uncertainty or difficult cases to staff or a stronger path.

feedback.Reason: The efficient design meets the stated performance and cost constraints, but quality still needs evidence. Routing difficult cases preserves service value without paying the agentic cost for routine traffic.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: A workload-specific benchmark links model pattern to latency, spend, quality, and escalation; the route makes a human or stronger path available where the efficient path is insufficient.
Details.scenarioApplication: Measure answer correctness, p95, cost per question, and escalation on routine and difficult slices before setting the efficient path as the default.
Details.errorCorrection: Align the architecture to the business value pillars and measured constraints instead of treating autonomy or price as a proxy for value.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The default path may automate fewer difficult cases, but it protects SLA and budget while generating evidence for a targeted upgrade.
Details.transfer: When choosing among AI designs, compare task quality, speed, spend, and operational workload on the slice that creates the proposed value.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Transformation language does not override a measured SLA and cost failure, and it provides no evidence that the extra autonomy helps the product-question task.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Price alone cannot establish useful answer quality or a safe default for customers.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Duplicate execution adds cost and answer length is not a business outcome or correctness measure.

items.prompt: A dashboard reports that 92% of conversations completed, but agents spend the same time because they rewrite many answers before sending them. Which measurement diagnosis should guide the next change?
constraints: Completion is high but does not reflect reviewer effort or outcome quality.
The current process can provide a baseline for resolution and handling time.

options.text: Increase the completion target to 98% and treat the higher percentage as proof that the assistant creates productivity.
Measure resolution, accepted-answer rate, handling time, and rework against the current process, segmented by conversation type.
Count generated words and use longer answers as evidence that the assistant addresses more customer needs.
Replace the model immediately because any rewriting means the AI path has no business value.

feedback.Reason: Completion is a weak proxy when human rewriting consumes the supposed time benefit. The next diagnosis must measure the actual work and outcome against current practice.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Resolution and acceptance capture usefulness, while handling time and rework capture productivity; segmentation shows where the assistant helps or burdens agents.
Details.scenarioApplication: Compare accepted answers, resolution and repeat contacts, minutes per case, and edits with a matched baseline before changing prompts or models.
Details.errorCorrection: Measure the business process end to end, including human correction, rather than optimizing a model-output or completion counter.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Richer measurement requires labeling and instrumentation, but it distinguishes a valuable draft from a fluent draft that adds work.
Details.transfer: Whenever a product metric stays high while users still work around the system, add outcome and effort measures tied to the current process.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Raising a proxy threshold does not address the unchanged handling time or reveal whether conversations actually resolve.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Generated volume can increase editing burden and says nothing about acceptance or customer outcome.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Rewriting identifies a possible defect but not whether a targeted prompt, route, or workflow change could recover value.

items.prompt: A research group seeks potentially transformational discovery across a changing corpus. Exploration is open-ended and a human must review evidence before any conclusion is acted on. Which value-aligned design should be piloted?
constraints: The opportunity depends on discovering new paths in a changing corpus.
Citations, budget limits, and human review are required before action.

options.text: Use a fixed retrieval workflow and publish its first answer as the discovery result so cost and latency remain predictable.
Open the full corpus to an unrestricted agent and let it act on a novel finding without an evidence or spending boundary.
Pilot an evaluated agentic research path with bounded searches, source citations, cost tracking, and human review of the proposed conclusion.
Optimize only the number of documents searched and treat broad corpus coverage as transformation regardless of finding quality.

feedback.Reason: Open-ended discovery is where adaptive exploration can create transformational value, but the pilot needs evidence, stop conditions, and human ownership before action.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: An agent can choose follow-up searches as findings change; budgets, source records, evaluation cases, and a human gate constrain the exploratory path.
Details.scenarioApplication: Measure discovery recall, citation support, time, spend, and reviewer acceptance on representative research tasks before expanding the pilot.
Details.errorCorrection: Match transformation claims to a measurable capability and preserve a review boundary for uncertain or consequential findings.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The evaluated pilot costs more and may leave findings pending review, but it tests the transformational hypothesis without making exploration an uncontrolled action path.
Details.transfer: For high-upside discovery, define the evidence, budget, and human decision boundary as part of the value case rather than as post-launch cleanup.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: A fixed path may be efficient but cannot adapt to the discovery-dependent work described and would publish without the required review.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Unrestricted exploration lacks a spending and evidence boundary and crosses the human action requirement.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Document count is an activity measure; it does not establish a useful discovery or supported conclusion.

items.prompt: A coding assistant produces many suggestions, but reviewers reject a large share and cleanup extends the engineering cycle. Which TWO measures should replace suggestion volume as the primary value signal? Select TWO.
constraints: Review and cleanup are part of the engineering work.
The goal is a faster, higher-quality end-to-end change process.

options.text: Accepted-change rate on representative suggestions, including the proportion merged with no substantive rewrite.
Total suggestions generated per developer, regardless of whether a change is accepted or useful.
Average response length, because longer code explanations indicate more capable assistance.
Number of files touched by each suggestion, even when reviewers revert the change.
End-to-end cycle time from request through review and rework to an accepted change, compared with the current workflow.

feedback.Reason: Accepted changes capture usefulness and cycle time captures the full productivity effect, including review and cleanup. Suggestion volume can rise while the process gets slower.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Outcome measures join model output to reviewer disposition and repository completion; a baseline comparison reveals whether assistance reduces total engineering effort.
Details.scenarioApplication: Track accepted-change rate by task type and elapsed request-to-merge time including review and rework against a matched non-assistant baseline.
Details.errorCorrection: Replace activity counts with measures that include human correction and the business process outcome the assistant is meant to improve.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The measures require review labels and longer observation windows, but they prevent a high-volume generator from appearing productive while increasing cycle time.
Details.transfer: For AI-assisted work, measure what users accept and how long the complete job takes, not how much text the model emits.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Suggestion volume rewards generation even when reviewers reject or rewrite the output and does not measure completed work.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Response length is not code quality or engineering productivity and can increase review burden.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Touched-file count can reflect noisy or harmful changes and has no relationship to accepted delivery time.

omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.a: Without accepted-change rate, the team cannot tell whether generated suggestions are useful enough to keep.
omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.e: Without end-to-end cycle time including review and rework, the dashboard can miss a productivity loss caused by cleanup.

items.prompt: A contact-center assistant reduces average handle time by 18%, but first-contact resolution falls from 84% to 72% and repeat contacts increase. The target is at least 82% first-contact resolution. What decision should follow?
constraints: The measured speed gain is paired with a material resolution regression.
The target resolution floor is 82% and slices can be evaluated before broad rollout.

options.text: Keep the release because handle-time improvement is the clearest efficiency signal, and address repeat contacts after adoption grows.
Roll back every AI feature permanently because one aggregate outcome regressed without testing where the regression occurs.
Pause broad expansion, segment the resolution failures, and retest a scoped prompt, retrieval, or human route until the 82% floor and acceptable handling time are jointly met.
Raise the resolution target in the dashboard to match the observed result while continuing the same design.

feedback.Reason: A faster interaction that fails to resolve the contact misses the service value target. The next step is a slice diagnosis and measured revision, not a single-metric rollout or an unscoped permanent rollback.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Segmented evaluation can locate failure classes such as policy gaps or unsafe confidence; routing, prompt, retrieval, or review changes can then be tested against both SLA pillars.
Details.scenarioApplication: Hold broad rollout, compare resolution and handle time by intent and customer segment, and accept a revised path only when it clears the 82% floor without unacceptable effort.
Details.errorCorrection: Treat speed and outcome quality as a joint business constraint and use failure slices to target the smallest corrective change.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Expansion pauses and analysis costs time, but it avoids scaling a fast workflow that drives repeat contacts and damages service value.
Details.transfer: When efficiency improves while outcome quality falls, keep both measures in the gate and diagnose the work slice before choosing rollout or redesign.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Handle time alone ignores the resolution target and accepts a workflow that shifts effort into repeat contacts.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: A full permanent rollback discards potentially recoverable value before identifying whether one slice or route causes the regression.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Changing the target hides a measured failure instead of bringing the service back to the agreed business floor.

items.prompt: An insurer pilots Claude summaries for adjusters. Managers want broader deployment, but the pilot has only summary acceptance data; adoption, time-to-decision, correction rate, and downstream claim outcomes were not measured. What value decision is appropriate?
constraints: The current evidence covers acceptance but not operational or downstream value.
Broader deployment can wait for a defined measurement gate.

options.text: Extend the pilot with measures for adjuster adoption, time-to-decision, correction rate, and downstream outcomes, then gate expansion on predefined thresholds.
Expand to every adjuster because acceptance of the summaries proves that the insurer will realize productivity value.
Stop measuring and select the model with the lowest token cost so the pilot cannot exceed budget.
Use the number of summaries generated as the expansion criterion and infer claim quality from coverage.

feedback.Reason: Acceptance is useful but incomplete. The business case concerns adoption, time, correction burden, and claim outcomes, so expansion needs a measurement gate for those effects.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: A pilot can connect summary versions to adjuster behavior, decision time, corrections, and later claim outcomes, producing a balanced value evaluation.
Details.scenarioApplication: Instrument representative adjusters and claim slices, compare with current practice, and expand only if quality remains acceptable while time and downstream outcomes improve.
Details.errorCorrection: Do not turn early approval into a broad productivity claim; define the operational and downstream measures before increasing exposure.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A longer pilot delays scale and requires outcome follow-up, but it protects the insurer from optimizing summaries that save no time or alter claim quality adversely.
Details.transfer: For AI features with indirect business effects, measure adoption, effort, corrections, and downstream outcomes before calling a pilot successful.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Acceptance does not establish adoption, time-to-decision, correction burden, or downstream claim quality at scale.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Token cost is one constraint and cannot replace the quality and operational measures needed for the business decision.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Generation volume measures activity, not whether adjusters use the summaries or whether claims resolve better.

items.prompt:
A tax-appeal assistant must recall at least 97% of material exceptions. The efficient model reaches 91%, while a stronger model reaches 98% at four times the unit cost and remains under the asynchronous service deadline.

Which model allocation satisfies the material-exception quality requirement?
constraints: The efficient model scores 91% and the stronger model 98% on the same held-out exception set.
At least 97% recall of material exceptions is required.
High-impact appeals are a minority and a human path remains available; the stronger route meets the asynchronous deadline.

options.text: Use the efficient model for all appeals because its lower cost maximizes productivity.
Use the stronger model for every appeal because quality is hard, and defer any cost or workload segmentation review.
Use the stronger route for exception cases, keeping the efficient model only where its measured quality clears the floor.
Route a random quarter of appeals to the stronger model and accept efficient output for the rest until an incident identifies a quality problem.

feedback.Reason: Value alignment can favor higher capability when a consequence-bearing quality floor is explicit and the route remains operationally feasible.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends evaluating model capabilities, speed, cost, and effort against the actual use case rather than optimizing one dimension alone. The scenario's mechanism is governed by this decisive constraint: The material-exception quality floor is a hard business requirement, so efficiency cannot justify a path that fails it.
Details.scenarioApplication: Use the stronger model for the exception workload or route it to a validated stronger or human path, and retain the efficient model only where its measured quality clears the applicable floor.
Details.errorCorrection: The efficient path misses the material-exception floor and shifts error cost into appeals without meeting the business outcome.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the efficient model cleared 97% on the same held-out slice, use it as the default and test a stronger route only for measured residual failures.
Details.transfer: Use measured evidence and the stated authority boundary to choose the least complex design that satisfies the workload's constraint; revisit the route when the counterfactual changes.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: The efficient path misses the material-exception floor and shifts error cost into appeals without meeting the business outcome.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: The stronger model clears the exception floor, but applying its four-times unit cost to every case ignores the stated minority workload and available allocation boundary.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Random sampling does not ensure the material-exception slice clears 97%; the measured failure is already known and should drive the route.

items.prompt:
A claims triage service handles 50,000 cases per month: 40,000 routine and 10,000 high-impact cases. On the same held-out routine and high-impact classes, the efficient model scores 97% and 91%, costs $0.02 per case, and runs at 1.2 seconds p95; the stronger model scores 98% and 96%, costs $0.15, and runs at 2.3 seconds p95.

Which model route satisfies the shared quality, latency, budget, and uncertainty constraints?
constraints: Both models were measured on the same routine and high-impact classes.
The high-impact floor is 95%, the service p95 limit is 2.5 seconds, and the monthly model budget is $2,500.
Classifier uncertainty has a reviewer path; the measured segmented route costs $2,300 and the stronger model is used for 10,000 high-impact cases.

options.text: Use the efficient model for all 50,000 cases because its $1,000 monthly cost is lowest.
Use the stronger model for every case because its 96% high-impact score clears the quality floor.
Route every case solely from the classifier, send no uncertainty cases to review, and accept the predicted class as the quality measure.
Route routine cases to the efficient model and high-impact cases to the stronger model, with budget, p95, quality, and reviewer gates.

feedback.Reason: The worked monthly costs and same-class outcomes make segmented routing the only stated design that meets the high-impact floor without exceeding budget or latency.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends evaluating model capabilities, speed, cost, and effort against the actual use case rather than optimizing one dimension alone. The scenario's mechanism is governed by this decisive constraint: Both models were measured on the same classes, so the decision must satisfy the 95% high-impact floor, 2.5-second p95 limit, and $2,500 monthly budget together.
Details.scenarioApplication: Use the efficient model for routine cases and the stronger model for identified high-impact cases, confirm the routed mix stays under the 2.5-second end-to-end p95 and $2,500 budget, and send classifier-uncertain high-impact cases to the bounded reviewer queue.
Details.errorCorrection: All-stronger exceeds the $2,500 budget by $5,000, while all-efficient misses the 95% high-impact floor; the stronger route is feasible at 2.3 seconds only for the high-impact slice.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the stronger route measured above 2.5 seconds end to end under the routed load, reject that route for the hard-deadline slice and use a reviewed asynchronous or narrower escalation path; if its cost fell below the global budget, broaden only after the same class gates pass.
Details.transfer: Use measured evidence and the stated authority boundary to choose the least complex design that satisfies the workload's constraint; revisit the route when the counterfactual changes.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: The efficient model scores only 91% on high-impact cases, below the 95% hard floor, so its lower cost cannot justify an all-efficient route.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: The all-stronger route costs $7,500 per month and exceeds the $2,500 budget even though its latency and quality are acceptable.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Classifier precision and predicted classes do not replace end-to-end slice quality; unresolved high-impact uncertainty needs the bounded reviewer path.
